_note: The M1 acceptance table (Spec §12.3, §13 M1) over the hand-written corpus beside it. It is data, not code, so `vsir demo exact --synthetic` and tests/api/test_acceptance_synthetic.py assert the same numbers. Nothing here may be re-baselined to make a run green (C10): a disagreement is a finding.

decoy.label: SF 1.1A
decoy.why: the tokens sf, 1 and 1a are all on p008 and none is adjacent to the next, so any-order matching returns it and a phrase does not (F1)

hallucinated.label: K999
hallucinated.why: claimed in content.codes, absent from text. Reachable only through unverified_hits, always verified:false (I2, F14, D3). No token of the label occurs anywhere in the text surface, so there is no move to suggest either.

no_text.label: SF 9.9
no_text.why: the only candidate page has no text layer: escalate to vision, never conclude the code does not exist (F4)

untrusted.label: K404
untrusted.why: text_trust: untrusted counts as unsearchable for lookup (§5.7), so the phrase in a garbled text layer is never a verified hit

weak.why: weak = total > max(WEAK_ABS, 0.25 * scope pages) — a server constant, so cap cannot move it (§7.1)

suggest.label: alarm 152
suggest.why: §12.3 — alarm is on p024, 152 is on p026, the phrase is nowhere. The status stays honest and the affordance stops the agent abstaining on a phrasing accident

asymmetric_variant.label: SF1.1A
asymmetric_variant.why: p001 prints the spaced form and variants() cannot produce it from the compact one: re-spacing a bare label spaces EVERY letter-digit boundary (SF 1.1 A), never just one. A recall gap by construction (§5.6, R1), and it degrades to an honest abstention carrying a next move — never to a wrong page

phrase_prefix.label: SF 1
phrase_prefix.why: a phrase match is a match on a contiguous run of tokens, so a SHORTER label whose spelling re-spaces into a prefix of a longer printed one is found: `SF 1` re-spaces to `sf 1`, which is printed inside `SF 1.1A`. Not fuzzy and not fabricated — the characters really are there — but it is the accepted cost of phrase semantics, because telling `SF 1` apart from the start of `SF 1.1A` needs an identifier grammar and §5.2 prohibits one. Recorded here so it is a known property; it is also why the §12.4 generator excludes candidates the corpus prints in ANY spelling

superseded.label: SF 7.7A
superseded.why: printed only on the is_current:false revision 0.9 page; every tool injects is_current:true (I7). F9 shipped at M8 and still reports not_found HERE: found_only_in_superseded names only revisions a run PUBLISHED, read from vsir_runs, and this corpus is seeded by a fixture loader with no run behind it. Naming 0.9 anyway would be the leak the control-plane check exists to prevent (U025)

superseded.label: K 158
superseded.why: printed on both revisions; only the current one can answer

out_of_scope.label: SF 1.1A
out_of_scope.why: no page matched the filters — re-orient and widen; the corpus was never asked (§7.1)

verify.why: §12.3's row — the tokens sf, 1 and 1a are all on p008 and the phrase is not. The one exact_filter answers `verify` and `lookup` identically, which is why F2 cannot disagree with F1
per (claim, page), not per claim: the verdict names the page that carries it, so a draft citing p002 cannot borrow p001's evidence (I8)
F16 — a prefix lookup over the observed tokens of that page, labelled `different part`, never a distance and never the match
I2 — the page claims it in content.codes and its text does not carry it, so the verdict is absent and there is nothing to disclose instead
§7.2.4 — collapsing this into `absent` would tell the agent the code is not on a page nobody could read
§5.7 — the phrase IS in that text layer, and the text layer is not evidence

I7 — a page that is not current cannot answer. `unverifiable` rather than `absent`, because the code may well be printed on it: the answer gate rejects the draft either way, and only this reading lets it tell a superseded citation from a scanned page

observed_tokens.why: §6.8 — built from the text surface of the 28 SEARCHABLE pages, and only from tokens carrying at least one digit. `k999` is excluded because it is only ever a model claim (I2); `k404` and `rai1` because they are printed only on the untrusted page, and a text layer nobody may be told is evidence must not volunteer codes either (§5.7); `eao84` because it is a spelling of a query variant and not a token anybody printed; bare words because the inventory exists to back `present_instead` and nothing else
